questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: According to VSEPR theory, the molecular geometry and point group of $\text{XeOF}_4$ are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{XeOF}_4$, xenon ($8$ valence electrons) forms one $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bond ($2$ electrons used), four $\text{Xe}-\text{F}$ single bonds ($4$ electrons used), and retains $1$ lone pair ($2$ electrons), giving a steric number of $6$ (octahedral electron-pair geometry). Placing the lone pair trans to the $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bond gives a square pyramidal molecular geometry belonging to the $C_{4v}$ point group. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Wade's skeletal electron pair (SEP) rules, the neutral icosahedral carborane $1,2\text{-C}_2\text{B}_{10}\text{H}_{12}$ is classified as a
questions.explanationEn: Each $\text{BH}$ vertex contributes $2$ skeletal electrons and each $\text{CH}$ vertex contributes $3$ skeletal electrons. For $\text{C}_2\text{B}_{10}\text{H}_{12}$ ($n = 12$ vertices), total skeletal electrons $= 2(3) + 10(2) = 26$, which equals $13$ skeletal electron pairs ($n + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13$). A polyhedral cluster with $n + 1$ SEPs adopts a closed *closo* (icosahedral) framework. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Magic acid is an equimolar mixture of $\text{HSO}_3\text{F}$ and $\text{SbF}_5$. Its extraordinary Brønsted superacidity arises because $\text{SbF}_5$ acts as a
optionsEn: strong Lewis acid that abstracts $\text{F}^-$ (or coordinates $\text{SO}_3\text{F}^-$) to form the weakly basic anion $[\text{SbF}_5(\text{SO}_3\text{F})]^-$, greatly increasing the activity of $[\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3\text{F}]^+$
strong Brønsted base that deprotonates alkanes directly
fluorinating agent that converts $\text{HSO}_3\text{F}$ into neutral $\text{SF}_6$
questions.explanationEn: In magic acid ($\text{HSO}_3\text{F}/\text{SbF}_5$), the powerful Lewis acid $\text{SbF}_5$ coordinates to the conjugate base $\text{SO}_3\text{F}^-$ via $2\text{HSO}_3\text{F} + \text{SbF}_5 \rightleftharpoons [\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3\text{F}]^+ + [\text{SbF}_5(\text{SO}_3\text{F})]^-$. Delocalizing the negative charge onto the large, extremely weakly basic counter-anion drives the equilibrium to generate highly reactive protonated fluorosulfuric acid ($H_0 \approx -23$). Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the seven crystal systems, the ONLY crystal system that possesses all four Bravais lattice centerings—primitive ($P$), body-centered ($I$), face-centered ($F$), and base-centered ($C$)—is
questions.explanationEn: The $14$ Bravais lattices are distributed across the $7$ crystal systems as: cubic ($P, I, F = 3$), tetragonal ($P, I = 2$), orthorhombic ($P, I, F, C = 4$), monoclinic ($P, C = 2$), triclinic ($P = 1$), rhombohedral/trigonal ($P/R = 1$), and hexagonal ($P = 1$). Only the orthorhombic crystal system has all four Bravais lattice types ($P, I, F, C$). Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Based on crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE), which of the following transition-metal oxides adopts a NORMAL spinel structure, $[\text{A}^{2+}]_{\text{tet}}[\text{B}^{3+}_2]_{\text{oct}}\text{O}_4$?
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{Co}_3\text{O}_4$ ($\text{Co}^{2+}\text{Co}^{3+}_2\text{O}_4$), oxide ions exert a strong enough field on the trivalent $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($d^6$) ion to make it low-spin ($t_{2g}^6$, $\text{CFSE} = -2.4\Delta_o$) in octahedral sites, imparting a massive octahedral site preference energy (OSPE). Thus $\text{Co}^{3+}$ occupies all octahedral sites and $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($d^7$) occupies tetrahedral sites, forming a normal spinel. By contrast, $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$, $\text{NiFe}_2\text{O}_4$, and $\text{CuFe}_2\text{O}_4$ are inverse spinels because high-spin $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($d^5$) has zero CFSE. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following interhalogen and noble-gas species, the molecule(s)/ion(s) that possess(es) a ZERO permanent dipole moment is(are)
questions.explanationEn: $\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{ICl}_4^-$ both have $4$ bonding pairs and $2$ trans lone pairs (steric number $6$), adopting centrosymmetric square planar ($D_{4h}$) geometries with zero net dipole moment (A and C are true). $\text{ClF}_3$ is T-shaped ($C_{2v}$) and $\text{SF}_4$ is seesaw-shaped ($C_{2v}$), so both are polar (B and D are false). Thus, (A) and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For ideal close-packed lattices of identical hard spheres (CCP/FCC and HCP), the CORRECT statement(s) is(are)
optionsEn: Both CCP (FCC) and HCP lattices have an identical packing efficiency of $\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{2}} \approx 74.05\%$.
Each sphere in both CCP and HCP has a coordination number of $12$.
Per $N$ close-packed spheres, there are $N$ octahedral voids and $2N$ tetrahedral voids.
The stacking sequence of close-packed layers is $\text{ABAB}\dots$ for FCC and $\text{ABCABC}\dots$ for HCP.
questions.explanationEn: Both FCC (CCP) and HCP are maximally dense sphere packings with $\text{CN} = 12$ (B is true), packing fraction $\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{2}} \approx 74.05\%$ (A is true), and $N$ octahedral plus $2N$ tetrahedral interstitial voids per $N$ atoms (C is true). However, FCC has the $\text{ABCABC}\dots$ stacking sequence while HCP has $\text{ABAB}\dots$ (D is reversed, hence false). Thus, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the *nido*-borane $\text{B}_5\text{H}_9$ (pentaborane-9), the total number of three-center two-electron ($3\text{c-}2\text{e}$) bonds (combining both $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ and $\text{B}-\text{B}-\text{B}$ $3\text{c-}2\text{e}$ bonds) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Pentaborane-9 ($\text{B}_5\text{H}_9$, square pyramidal *nido* structure) has Lipscomb *styx* number $4120$: $s = 4$ bridging $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ $3\text{c-}2\text{e}$ bonds, $t = 1$ $\text{B}-\text{B}-\text{B}$ $3\text{c-}2\text{e}$ bond, $y = 2$ direct $\text{B}-\text{B}$ $2\text{c-}2\text{e}$ bonds, and $x = 0$ $\text{BH}_2$ groups. Notice that by Lipscomb's topological balance equation $s + t = p$ (number of boron atoms), so $s + t = 4 + 1 = 5$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the tetraborate anion $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$ present in crystalline borax ($\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$), the total number of $\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ bridges is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: The tetraborate anion $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$ consists of two $sp^2$ trigonal planar boron atoms and two $sp^3$ tetrahedral boron atoms. Four terminal $-\text{OH}$ groups are attached (one to each boron), while the five remaining $\text{O}$ atoms act as bridging oxygens: four form the outer $8$-membered $\text{B}_4\text{O}_4$ ring and one bridges the two tetrahedral boron centers across the ring. Thus, there are $5$ $\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ bridges.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Gold crystallizes in a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with a unit cell edge length $a = 408\text{ pm}$. The metallic radius of a gold atom (in $\text{pm}$) is _____ (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanationEn: In an FCC unit cell, atoms touch along the face diagonal, so $\sqrt{2}a = 4r \implies r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$. Substituting $a = 408\text{ pm}$ gives $r = \frac{408}{2 \times 1.41421} = \frac{408}{2.82843} = 144.2\text{ pm}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Using Wade's rules, the structural classifications (*closo*, *nido*, or *arachno*) of the three clusters $\text{C}_2\text{B}_9\text{H}_{11}^{2-}$, $\text{SB}_{11}\text{H}_{11}$, and $\text{B}_5\text{H}_{11}$ are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: Count skeletal electron pairs (SEPs) using $\text{BH} = 2\text{e}$, $\text{CH} = 3\text{e}$, $\text{S} = 4\text{e}$ (since $\text{S}$ has $6$ valence electrons minus $2$ for an exo lone pair): (1) $[\text{C}_2\text{B}_9\text{H}_{11}]^{2-}$ ($n = 11$): $2(3) + 9(2) + 2 = 26\text{e} = 13\text{ SEPs} = n + 2 \implies$ *nido* (dicarbollide anion). (2) $\text{SB}_{11}\text{H}_{11}$ ($n = 12$): $4 + 11(2) = 26\text{e} = 13\text{ SEPs} = n + 1 \implies$ *closo*. (3) $\text{B}_5\text{H}_{11}$ ($n = 5$): $\text{B}_n\text{H}_{n+6} \implies 8\text{ SEPs} = n + 3 \implies$ *arachno*. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Regarding xenon hexafluoride ($\text{XeF}_6$), which of the following statements is CORRECT?
optionsEn: In the gas phase, $\text{XeF}_6$ is a rigid regular octahedron ($O_h$) with a stereochemically inactive lone pair.
$\text{XeF}_6$ acts exclusively as a fluoride acceptor and never donates $\text{F}^-$ to Lewis acids.

In the gas phase, $\text{XeF}_6$ is a fluxional distorted octahedron (monocapped octahedron, $C_{3v}$), and with $\text{CsF}$ it forms the fluoride-acceptor salt $\text{Cs}^+[\text{XeF}_7]^-$ (or $\text{Cs}_2[\text{XeF}_8]$).
In the solid state, $\text{XeF}_6$ consists of isolated planar hexagonal rings.
questions.explanationEn: In the gas phase, $\text{XeF}_6$ has $6$ bonding pairs and $1$ stereochemically active lone pair, adopting a fluxional distorted octahedral ($C_{3v}$ monocapped octahedral) geometry. It is amphoteric toward $\text{F}^-$: it acts as a fluoride donor with $\text{SbF}_5$ to form $[\text{XeF}_5]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$, and as a fluoride acceptor with $\text{CsF}$ to form $\text{Cs}[\text{XeF}_7]$ and $\text{Cs}_2[\text{XeF}_8]$. In the solid state, it forms fluoride-bridged tetramers and hexamers of $[\text{XeF}_5^+\text{F}^-]$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the interhalogen series $\text{XY}_n$ (where $\text{X}$ is the heavier, less electronegative halogen), why does $\text{IF}_7$ exist as a stable molecular compound whereas $\text{ClF}_7$ and $\text{IBr}_7$ do not?
optionsEn: Iodine has a higher electronegativity than chlorine, stabilizing seven bonds.

A high radius ratio $r_{\text{X}}/r_{\text{Y}}$ (large central $\text{I}$ and small peripheral $\text{F}$) minimizes steric crowding, and $\text{F}$ is electronegative enough to oxidize $\text{I}$ to $+7$.
$\text{IF}_7$ is stabilized by strong $\text{F}-\text{F}$ covalent bonds around the equatorial belt.
Chlorine cannot expand its octet beyond four bonds in any fluoride.
questions.explanationEn: Attaining a high coordination number ($n = 7$) requires both a large central atom $\text{X}$ and small, strongly oxidizing peripheral ligands $\text{Y}$ to minimize steric repulsion and stabilize the $+7$ oxidation state. Iodine with fluorine provides the largest $r_{\text{X}}/r_{\text{Y}}$ ratio and highest oxidizing power, allowing $\text{IF}_7$ ($D_{5h}$, pentagonal bipyramidal) to exist, whereas $\text{Cl}$ is too small for seven $\text{F}$ atoms and $\text{Br}$ is both too large and too weak an oxidant for $\text{IBr}_7$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a stoichiometric $\text{MX}$ ionic crystal with $N$ cation sites and $N$ anion sites, the enthalpy of formation of one Schottky defect pair (one cation vacancy + one anion vacancy) is $\Delta H_S$. At temperature $T$ (assuming $n_S \ll N$ and neglecting vibrational entropy), the equilibrium number of Schottky defect pairs $n_S$ is given by
questions.explanationEn: The configurational entropy of distributing $n_S$ cation vacancies among $N$ cation sites and $n_S$ anion vacancies among $N$ anion sites is $S = k_B \ln\left[\frac{N!}{(N-n_S)!n_S!}\right]^2$. Minimizing $G = n_S \Delta H_S - TS$ using Stirling's approximation gives $\Delta H_S - 2k_B T \ln\left(\frac{N - n_S}{n_S}\right) = 0$. For $n_S \ll N$, this yields $n_S = N \exp\left(-\frac{\Delta H_S}{2k_B T}\right)$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an ideal hexagonal close-packed (HCP) crystal made of identical rigid spheres, the ratio of the unit cell height $c$ to the basal edge length $a$ ($c/a$) is
questions.explanationEn: In an ideal HCP structure, three touching spheres in layer A form an equilateral triangle of side $a = 2r$, and a sphere in layer B rests in the hollow above them to form a regular tetrahedron of edge $a$. The height of a regular tetrahedron of edge $a$ is $h = a\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$. Since the unit cell spans two layer intervals ($\text{A} \to \text{B} \to \text{A}$), $c = 2h = a\sqrt{\frac{8}{3}}$, giving $\frac{c}{a} = \sqrt{\frac{8}{3}} \approx 1.633$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following bond-angle or structural comparisons are CORRECTLY explained by Bent's rule and VSEPR theory?
optionsEn: The bond angle in $\text{OF}_2$ ($103^\circ$) is smaller than in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($104.5^\circ$) because electronegative $\text{F}$ increases $p$-character in the $\text{O}-\text{F}$ bonds.
In $\text{PF}_3\text{Cl}_2$, the axial $\text{P}-\text{F}$ bonds are longer than the equatorial $\text{P}-\text{F}$ bond.
In $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{PH}_3$, and $\text{AsH}_3$, the $\text{H}-\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond angle increases steadily down Group $15$.
In $\text{SF}_4$, the axial $\text{S}-\text{F}$ bonds are longer than the equatorial $\text{S}-\text{F}$ bonds.
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{OF}_2$, $\text{F}$ is more electronegative than $\text{H}$, pulling $p$-character into $\text{O}-\text{F}$ bonds and narrowing $\angle\text{FOF}$ relative to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (A is true). In trigonal bipyramidal $\text{PF}_3\text{Cl}_2$ and seesaw $\text{SF}_4$, axial bonds have lower $s$-character (more $p$/$3\text{c-}4\text{e}$ character) and greater $90^\circ$ repulsions than equatorial bonds, making axial bonds longer (B and D are true). Down Group $15$, $\angle\text{HEH}$ decreases ($\text{NH}_3: 107^\circ > \text{PH}_3: 93.5^\circ > \text{AsH}_3: 91.8^\circ$; C is false). Thus, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The CORRECT geometry/point-group assignment(s) for xenon oxides and oxyfluorides is(are)
optionsEn: $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$: seesaw ($C_{2v}$) with both $\text{F}$ atoms axial and both $\text{O}$ atoms equatorial
questions.explanationEn: Checking VSEPR structures: $\text{XeO}_3$ has $3$ $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ bonds + $1$ lone pair $\implies$ trigonal pyramidal $C_{3v}$ (A is true); $\text{XeO}_4$ has $4$ $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ bonds + $0$ lone pairs $\implies$ tetrahedral $T_d$ (B is true); $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ has $2$ $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$, $2$ $\text{Xe}-\text{F}$, and $1$ lone pair (steric number $5$), placing the lone pair and double-bonded oxygens equatorially and electronegative fluorines axially to give a seesaw $C_{2v}$ structure (C is true). $\text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2$ has $5$ bonding domains and $0$ lone pairs, so it is trigonal bipyramidal ($D_{3h}$), not square pyramidal (D is false). Thus, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Regarding non-aqueous solvent systems and Lewis acid-base chemistry, the CORRECT statement(s) is(are)
optionsEn: In liquid $\text{SO}_2$ ($2\text{SO}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{SO}^{2+} + \text{SO}_3^{2-}$), $\text{SOCl}_2$ behaves as an acid and $\text{Cs}_2\text{SO}_3$ behaves as a base.
Fluoroantimonic acid ($\text{HF}/\text{SbF}_5$) can protonate saturated hydrocarbons such as methane to form the methanium ion $\text{CH}_5^+$.
In the Lux-Flood acid-base definition, $\text{CaO}$ is an acid and $\text{SiO}_2$ is a base.
In liquid $\text{BrF}_3$, $\text{KF}$ acts as a base (forming $\text{K}^+[\text{BrF}_4]^-$) whereas $\text{SbF}_5$ acts as an acid (forming $[\text{BrF}_2]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$).
questions.explanationEn: In liquid $\text{SO}_2$, $\text{SOCl}_2$ furnishes $\text{SO}^{2+}$ (acid) and $\text{Cs}_2\text{SO}_3$ furnishes $\text{SO}_3^{2-}$ (base; A is true). $\text{HF}/\text{SbF}_5$ ($H_0 \approx -28$) protonates $\text{CH}_4$ to $\text{CH}_5^+$ (B is true). In liquid $\text{BrF}_3$ ($2\text{BrF}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{BrF}_2^+ + \text{BrF}_4^-$), $\text{KF}$ donates $\text{F}^-$ to produce $\text{BrF}_4^-$ (base) and $\text{SbF}_5$ abstracts $\text{F}^-$ to produce $\text{BrF}_2^+$ (acid; D is true). By the Lux-Flood definition (oxide transfer), $\text{CaO}$ is an oxide donor (base) and $\text{SiO}_2$ is an oxide acceptor (acid; C is false). Thus, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
Copper (atomic mass $= 63.55\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) crystallizes in a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with a unit cell edge length $a = 3.615\text{ \AA}$. The theoretical density of copper (in $\text{g cm}^{-3}$) is _____ (rounded off to two decimal places).
[Given: $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: For an FCC lattice, $Z = 4$ atoms per unit cell and $a = 3.615 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}$, so $a^3 = 4.7242 \times 10^{-23}\text{ cm}^3$. Using $\rho = \frac{Z M}{N_A a^3}$: $\rho = \frac{4 \times 63.55}{(6.022 \times 10^{23})(4.7242 \times 10^{-23})} = \frac{254.20}{28.449} = 8.94\text{ g cm}^{-3}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Main Group & Solid State Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
Using the Born-Landé equation, the magnitude of the lattice energy $|U_0|$ (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) of $\text{NaCl}$ (Madelung constant $M = 1.748$, equilibrium nearest-neighbor distance $r_0 = 2.82\text{ \AA}$, Born exponent $n = 8$) is _____ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
[Given: $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 8.988 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^2\text{ C}^{-2}$]
questions.explanationEn: By the Born-Landé equation, $|U_0| = \frac{N_A M |z_+ z_-| e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r_0}\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)$. Substituting $M = 1.748$, $|z_+ z_-| = 1$, $r_0 = 2.82 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}$, and $1 - \frac{1}{8} = 0.875$: $|U_0| = \frac{(6.022 \times 10^{23})(1.748)(8.988 \times 10^9)(1.602 \times 10^{-19})^2}{2.82 \times 10^{-10}} \times 0.875 = 7.535 \times 10^5\text{ J mol}^{-1} \approx 753\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
